program: Violence interruption, youth opportunity and community support
priceScope: Full annual recipient cost against conditional injury-response, completed-therapy and youth-workforce channels; not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift EV.
what: Struggle of Love provides violence interruption, trauma support and school-based mentorship in Northeast Denver and North Aurora.
It also operates food distribution and youth employment opportunities.
Its teams connect families to counseling, crisis support and other community providers.
strengths: Local BIPOC-led organization with direct crisis and neighborhood access.
The 2024 report distinguishes shooting incidents, therapy completions and paid youth placements.
Food, employment and mental-health support address more than one pathway to household welfare.
reservations: Incident responses and paid placements do not establish incremental health or earnings gains.
Controlled violence-intervention evidence is uncertain and differs from SOL’s model.
Full annual costs cover several unquantified channels, so the displayed partial-channel reference is not a portfolio ranking.

sections.what: Struggle of Love provides violence interruption, trauma support and school-based mentorship in Northeast Denver and North Aurora. It also operates food distribution and youth employment opportunities. Its teams connect families to counseling, crisis support and other community providers.
sections.monitoring: The 2024 report describes 105 shooting incidents responded to, 30 therapy completions or successful discharges, 25 concession-employed youth and ten additional public youth-employment placements. Food pounds, STAR referrals and center visits are not unique causal outcomes. The 30 completed therapy clients form a separate conditional clinical channel; potential shared benefits with incident response are overlap-discounted rather than presumed independent. The next useful monitoring asks for unique completed clients, local residence, actual additional gains and costs; contacts and satisfaction are not causal outcomes.
sections.qualitative: The numerical reference hypothesizes one exposed person per shooting incident, 20% recipient contribution, a 5% additional injury-risk reduction and 0.1 QALY per avoided nonfatal injury. These are judgments, not measured SOL effects. A 130-person hospital-based pilot RCT found a 10.4 percentage-point repeat-injury difference with p=.15; a null or harmful result remains plausible. The distinct 25-person concession-workforce envelope uses 30% additional employment and $500 net annual household gain after taxes, benefit withdrawals and ordinary work costs, with $50 additional participation cost on every household and conservative positive overlap. Public placements, alternative jobs, employers and other support organizations matter. There is no child lifetime-wage or retail food-income claim. Separately, 30 completed/discharged therapy clients receive a conditional 0.03 QALY one-year improvement (10.95 healthy-day equivalents), 20% additionality and 50% positive clinical overlap reduction. The original Resick randomized trauma-therapy trial establishes symptom improvement against minimal attention, not a utility conversion, SOL fidelity or superiority to active local care. The utility hypothesis remains unmeasured and tested at zero. Therapy access costs $20 on all completed-client households, jointly netted with job costs in an explicit overlap sensitivity; no additional therapy earnings are assumed.
sections.cost: The full FY2024 recipient expense is $3,006,875. Unmeasured therapy causal magnitude, pantry and broader coalition contributions remain unknown, not zero, and the model does not estimate whole-portfolio or next-gift expected value. A $30/hour sensitivity for 3,720 volunteer hours adds shadow resources without asserting a household payer loss. Giving goes through the recipient’s own ColoradoGives link; no donation was executed.
sections.funding: The three full-year original expense figures are disclosed below. Current marginal donor capacity, public-provider substitution and restricted program allocations are not established by these filings.

sources: Original youth injury pilot randomized trial

sourcePublishers.therapy-trial: Resick et al., Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology

costScope: Full FY2024 organizational expenses, not allocated injury-response or job-placement costs.
geography: Northeast Denver and North Aurora service area is within pinned ten-county Denver CBSA19740; .98 recipient-benefit share is a judgment allowing outside residents.
formula: Health = incident envelope × patient-per-incident hypothesis × additionality × injury-risk response × finite QALY burden, less full incident-exposure harms. Separate workforce household joint logs include full costs and positive-only overlap; price = 10 × annual cost / (health + signed resource equivalent). A separate 30-person therapy clinical hypothesis adds finite benefit with positive clinical overlap reduction and full client harms; therapy/job household costs jointly logged if overlapping.
counterfactual: Other community, hospital and public violence response; publicly supported youth placements, ordinary jobs and other family resources.
attribution: Recipient contribution .2 for injury prevention and job additionality .3 are separate hypotheses; they are not inferred from partner STAR totals.
uncertainty: Primary pilot trial does not establish injury reduction; recipient injury severity, unique people, net wages, donor capacity and portfolio cost allocation remain unknown.
native: 105 incident responses; 25 concession-employed youth; ten public placements; 30 therapy completions/discharges; 3,720 volunteer hours in the 2024 report.
nativeUnit: annual shooting incidents responded to, not observed unique patients

inputRationales.C: Observed full FY2024 original IRS organizational expenses, no netted event/gaming/inventory additions identified.
inputRationales.N: Observed 105 shooting incident responses in the 2024 annual report. One exposed patient per incident is a separate explicit hypothesis.
inputRationales.resourceN: Observed 25 concession-employed youth; unique household conversion and incremental job probability are judgments.
inputRationales.q: Judgment 0.1 finite QALY per avoided nonfatal violent injury, not a measured trial utility or mortality benefit.
inputRationales.response: Judgment 5% risk reduction; original pilot 10.4-point difference had p=.15 and is not transferred as proven efficacy.
inputRationales.therapyN: Observed 30 full therapy completions or successful discharges in 2024; completion is not clinical response.
inputRationales.therapyQ: Judgment 0.03 QALY over one year, 10.95 healthy-day equivalents; original trauma trial measured symptoms, not utilities, and SOL case mix/fidelity is unknown.
